center_definition: oblique subtalar axis, inclined about 42 degrees from the transverse plane and deviated about 16 degrees medially from the long axis of the foot
coupled_motion_notes: A single oblique axis converts leg rotation into hindfoot inversion/eversion and vice versa -- the mechanism that couples the foot to the rest of the limb during stance. Motion here is triplanar, so 'inversion' is a combined supination-adduction-plantarflexion rather than a pure frontal plane rotation.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); AAOS Joint Motion: Method of Measuring and Recording (1965)

center_definition: combined talonavicular and calcaneocuboid joint line
coupled_motion_notes: Its two component joints have parallel axes when the hindfoot is everted, which unlocks the midfoot, and divergent axes when inverted, which locks it into a rigid lever for push-off. This locking mechanism is why the windlass and the subtalar position govern midfoot stiffness together.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
